task: Automate cross-ticket attachment transfer and OCR-based text extraction when creating Jira bugs from support requests.

key_reasoning.reason: GenericJiraIssueTool requires 3+ new methods (_download_all_attachments, _copy_attachments_to_issue, _extract_and_append_image_text), JiraConfig needs a structural chat_model field addition, tools_vars.py docstring must be updated, and optionally a new JiraAttachmentContentMixin introduced; the tool is registered in 8+ prebuilt assistant definitions giving any change a wide blast radius across multiple agents.

Multiple open design decisions: 'no fidelity loss' directly conflicts with the hard-coded 5 MB per-image cap; 'logged/auditable' is ambiguous between transient logger.info calls and durable SkillEventRepository writes; OCR text injection target (edit bug description vs POST /comment) is unspecified; handling of non-image attachments (PDFs, ZIPs) for the copy pipeline is undefined; separate size/count caps for copy vs display are undecided.

Cross-ticket attachment download-then-upload is a new data flow with no existing Jira-domain implementation; _handle_file_attachments has zero test coverage making it a fragile foundation; wiring ImageProcessor into GenericJiraIssueTool requires a structural change to JiraConfig (adding chat_model); partial-failure handling per attachment adds error-handling complexity; the Azure DevOps AttachmentContentMixin reference pattern requires adaptation, not direct reuse.

Changes span Agent-Tool layer (GenericJiraIssueTool new methods + execute dispatch), Utility layer (ImageProcessor wired into Jira tool for first time), Config layer (JiraConfig structural change + module constants promoted), and External layer (new Jira REST API patterns: GET /issue/{key}?fields=attachment, POST /issue/{key}/attachments, POST /issue/{key}/comment); durable audit scope would additionally touch Repository/Service layer.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L(4) to XL(5): GenericJiraIssueTool is registered in 8+ prebuilt assistant definitions — new behavior affects multiple agents simultaneously

Requirements Clarity bumped from M(3) to L(4): vague acceptance criteria — 'no fidelity loss' conflicts with the existing 5 MB hard-coded image cap; 'logged/auditable' has no defined implementation scope (transient vs durable)
